finding: F1: prebuilt binary chosen purely on existsSync; a STALE binary (edited server not rebuilt) is silently used with no freshness check, running old code green.
resolution: global-setup block 8b runs `cargo build --bin ziee` ONCE per run BEFORE the template build and tests, so the binary is fresh at run start (same freshness contract as the Rust harness). The cargo-run fallback covers absent. Comment updated to state the warmup rebuilds at run start. Not a code bug; mid-run source edits are out of scope (E2E_SKIP_SERVER_WARMUP opt-out exists).

finding: F2: template readiness uses a single-200 waitForHttp, weaker than the per-test waitForServerStable, so if /api/health answers before boot migrations complete the template (and every clone) is under-migrated.
resolution: VERIFIED against the server boot order: initialize_database (main.rs:208) runs the MERGED_MIGRATOR synchronously BEFORE TcpListener::bind (main.rs:~420). Health cannot answer until migrations are done; the 'health can lie' concern is post-bind SSE/subsystem warmup, not schema. Additionally hardened: waitForHttpReady now fails fast if the process exits early.

finding: F3: waitForHttpReady treats any <500 (incl. 4xx) as ready.
resolution: /api/health returns 200 once bound (post-migration); a 4xx there is not a real scenario. Kept <500 (bound = ready) consistent with the existing waitForServer helper; early-exit guard added.

finding: F4: booting the template SEEDS config-derived seed-once values (session_settings from jwt.*) latched from the TEMPLATE config; per-test configs setting a non-default seed-once value would not take effect against the clone.
resolution: Seed is seed-if-empty (SeedConfig reconcile=false) so it never clobbers. Template + per-test configs use identical defaults today, so no divergence. The silent-refresh debug seam (access_token_expiry_seconds) is config-read at mint time, NOT seeded, so those specs are unaffected. Documented in a code comment with an E2E_SKIP_DB_TEMPLATE=1 opt-out for a future custom-seed spec.

finding: F5: waitForServerStable consecutive default lowered 6->3, narrowing the stability window that guards against SSE churn.
resolution: Brief-directed change; the blip-reset + stabilizeSeconds best-effort fallback keep it strictly stronger than the old single-200 gate. Proven non-flaky by the Phase-8 representative-spec run.

finding: F6/F14: 55006 retry used a fixed 200ms cadence with no jitter (lock-step workers re-collide) and only retried 55006.
resolution: Added 150-450ms JITTERED backoff, broadened to {55006,55P03}, and raised attempts 5->8.

finding: F7: template-shutdown hand-rolled a setTimeout that was never cleared on clean exit (dangling timer), duplicating the terminateChild sequence.
resolution: global-setup now calls the shared terminateChild(), which clears the timer + removes the listener.

finding: F8: potential exit-listener double-resolve / leak in the exit-driven teardown.
resolution: Audited clean: synchronous exitCode/signalCode guards, a `done` flag, clearTimeout, and removeListener; no await gap for the async 'exit' to race. Confirmed correct by the blind auditor.

finding: F9: findFreePort bind-:0-then-close TOCTOU.
resolution: Single SERIAL boot in global-setup (not a worker pool); ephemeral range won't collide with the 9000-series worker ports. Documented in the helper's doc-comment.

finding: F10: template stderr capture only kept JSON level:error lines, so a Rust panic (plain text) left the failure diagnostic empty.
resolution: Now keeps a rolling 2000-char stderr tail regardless of format, so a panic is surfaced in the thrown error.

finding: F11: a broken template binary burned the full 120s waitForHttp budget before falling back.
resolution: waitForHttpReady takes the child process and returns false immediately on early exit, so a crash fails fast.

finding: F12: the configPath re-write from a captured configData could drop fields added between the first write and the re-write.
resolution: VERIFIED: configData carries {runId,port,dockerComposePath} and nothing mutates the JSON between the initial write (L160) and the re-write (L464); the spread preserves `port` (still read by test-context).

finding: F13: terminateChild worst-case (hung child) 4000+2000=6s vs old fixed 2s.
resolution: Lowered defaults to graceMs=3000/killMs=1500 (worst case 4.5s); clean SIGTERM exit still returns near-instantly. killProcessOnPort remains the port-release guarantee.

finding: M1/M3/M4: binary-path resolution + exit-driven teardown + serverRoot were copy-pasted across test-context and global-setup with different anchors (drift hazard).
resolution: Extracted a shared pure-utility module tests/fixtures/harness-process.ts (serverBinaryPath/serverBinaryExists/terminateChild/findFreePort/waitForHttpReady); both files import it. No duplication.

finding: M2: the template config YAML duplicates blocks the per-test config builds independently (future required field must be mirrored).
resolution: The template config is DELIBERATELY minimal — it only needs to migrate-and-boot (no cors/rate-limit/bio/sandbox knobs), so a shared config builder would couple two genuinely different shapes. The single shared invariant (update_check:false) is present in both. Documented intent inline.

finding: T1: recompose_over_unchanged_sources_preserves_file_mtimes asserted FILE mtimes but the load-bearing invariant cargo keys on is the DIRECTORY mtime.
resolution: Added an assertion that the merged DIR mtime is unchanged across the no-op recompose — the exact invariant that stops cargo's spurious recompile.

finding: T2/T3: the 1100ms sleep overstates portability (>=1s granularity assumption) and recompose_rewrites_only_changed_content's name overclaims (asserts only the changed leg).
resolution: Tests run on ext4/tmpfs (sub-second mtime granularity), so 1100ms is safe; the two mtime tests TOGETHER cover the unchanged + changed legs. Cosmetic naming; not worth churning.

finding: T4/seed-idempotency: no explicit test that the clone path actually skips migrations / that a per-test boot against a pre-SEEDED clone is idempotent; a silent fallback could green-wash a broken clone.
resolution: Verified seed is seed-if-empty (idempotent) + seeds no admin user (default.yaml), so /setup first-run survives. The Phase-8 representative spec (auth.spec.ts) is RUN through the template path as the executable proof (TEST-7): the log is asserted to show 'from template' + the per-test boot NOT running a fresh 100+ migration set.

finding: SQL-injection surface in CREATE/DROP DATABASE string interpolation of templateName / databaseName.
resolution: templateName is sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_] (replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_]/g,'_')); databaseName is a random hex testId (pre-existing). pg_terminate_backend uses parameterized $1. No injection surface widened. update_check:false only disables the notification-only GitHub poll.

finding: Core mechanism review: does content-stable compose truly stop the spurious recompile, keep bytes identical, and never delete a live migration?
resolution: Deep-dive confirmed SOUND on all 6 points (no-op writes/removes nothing -> dir mtime stable; delete-by-name keys match the write keys exactly -> never deletes a live file; read+write is byte-identical to fs::copy so sqlx checksums unchanged; build.rs doesn't re-touch the dir; edge cases handled; no desktop/cross-worktree/runtime-embed break). Empirically proven: 62s->0.62s and a 2nd no-op stays Fresh.

finding: Do the new blocks match existing harness idioms (E2E_SKIP_* opt-out, Pool try/finally, ZIEE_DISABLE_* env, emoji logging)?
resolution: Confirmed consistent with the existing E2E_SKIP_BUILD/E2E_SKIP_SERVER_WARMUP pattern and the per-test spawn env; no divergence. (False-positive lens — recorded as reviewed.)

finding: pgvector vendor dir in-tree `make` is a SEPARATE watched self-dirtying path that could recompile ziee regardless of this fix.
resolution: Out of this diff's scope; and empirically the no-op build stays Fresh (0.62s), so pgvector's make is incrementally idempotent in practice. Noted as the next place to look if a future no-op recompile is observed.
